description: Optimal landmark cost partitioning gives each pending landmark a value `c_l` and maximizes their sum with a linear program (*LP*). A *landmark* is a fact that is true at some point of every plan. The LP has one constraint per operator: the values of the landmarks it achieves add up to at most its cost. So the sum never overestimates the cost of a plan (it is *admissible*), and it is never below the uniform partitioning. The crate solves one LP per state with the pure-Rust `microlp` (feature `lp`); it suits optimal search on small tasks and comparisons, while LM-cut is much cheaper per state.

papers.title: Cost-Optimal Planning with Landmarks
papers.venue: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI)
